chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir narrated from his paternal uncle 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Muqatil ibn Sulayman, who said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said:

When Musa (peace be upon him) ascended to Mount Sinai and called upon his Lord, the Mighty and High, he said: 'O Lord, show me your treasures.' He replied: 'O Musa, My treasure is that when I intend something, I say to it: Be, and it is.'

The compiler of this book says: Among the proofs that Allah, the Mighty and High, is Omnipotent is: since it is established that the Creator made the world, and we do not find that He creates what He is not capable of creating, as evidenced that the seated one cannot walk and the incapable cannot perform an action, it is correct that the One who created it is Omnipotent. If something other than this were possible, then it would be possible for us to fly without the necessary instrument, and for us to perceive without the senses. Since the possibility of the latter is contrary to reason, so is the former.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of God's 'treasure' in the hadith of Musa (AS) and how does it prove omnipotence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS narrates that Musa (AS) asked God to show Him His treasures, and God replied that His treasure is the power of command ('Be, and it is'). The compiler then provides a theological argument for God's omnipotence, stating that since the world was created by a capable Creator, and impossibility (like a seated person walking) is distinct from capability, God's power is absolute. If the opposite were true, logical contradictions would arise, such as flying without wings.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 17. Ja`far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (RA) said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn `Amir said, on the authority of his paternal uncle `Abd Allah ibn `Amir, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, on the authority of Maqatil ibn Sulayman that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said:

When Musa (AS) went to Mount Sinai. He called unto his Lord, the Mighty and High, “O Lord, show me your treasures!” Thus, Allah replied, “O Musa! Verily, My Treasure is that when I intend something, I say to it: `Be and it is.’”

The Compiler of this book (RA) says: Among the proofs upon the Omnipotence of Allah, the Mighty and High, is: the world is a creation of the Creator, since things can only be created by One who is Omnipotent. The disabled cannot walk, and the incapable cannot carry out actins. Hence, it is correct to say that one who created the world is Omnipotent. If something other than this is possible then it would be possible for us to fly without wings, and to perceive without the senses. And therefore, if the possibility of the latter is against logic, then so is the first.
